meta.falsification: A verified model would settle the question (677 would have a model of order 12); a rejected proof would expose an error.
meta.hypothesis: No model is found within 200,000 conflicts per case; most cases are refuted and the difficulty is concentrated in a small set (an exploratory triage found 57 hard cases).
meta.methodology: Run all 195 cases (3 worker processes, fixed order of results); certify UNSAT cases; verify any model on its table; list the UNKNOWN cases with their CNF hashes.
meta.question: Which of the 195 case CNFs of Lemma 8 for law 677 at order 12 can be refuted cheaply, with a certificate, and which remain?
meta.title: Law 677 at order 12: certified reduction of the 195 case CNFs to the hard ones

summary: 677 at order 12: 195 cases; refuted and certified by drat-trim: 138 of 138 UNSAT; models found: 0; undecided within 200000 conflicts: 57 (14 idempotent, 43 non-idempotent)
so 677 has a model of order 12 iff one of the listed hard case CNFs is satisfiable
